title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
This incident is an impersonation fraud in which scammers used AI-generated images and videos to fabricate a false identity as a real, named attorney. The failure did not originate inside a legitimate AI deployment. Instead, bad actors used generative AI tools to produce synthetic media at scale, creating hundreds of fake social media profiles and videos presenting themselves as an established legal professional. The point of harm was the social media platforms where the content circulated and where victims were recruited before being directed to payment apps.

Catching this kind of fraud requires either platform-level detection of AI-generated synthetic media impersonating real individuals, or rapid-response removal systems once abuse is reported. The volume reported here, nearly 6,500 profiles removed across multiple platforms, indicates that no such detection was operating effectively in advance. Removal was reactive, driven by the real attorney hiring a third-party anti-piracy firm rather than by any platform acting independently.

What is not established is who the individual scammers are, whether any law enforcement action has been taken against them, or whether the payment platforms had any knowledge of the fraudulent transactions.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the target of artificial intelligence scammers who are stealing his identity to defraud vulnerable immigrants. Criminals have created hundreds of fake videos and social media profiles using AI-generated images and videos of Leal, falsely offering immigration services such as US residency assistance for cash payments of around $2,200. The problem has escalated dramatically in recent months, with scammers directing potential victims through WhatsApp to send money via payment apps like Venmo, Zelle, and Cash App.

After first noticing suspicious activity last October, the situation spiraled out of control over the past three months when potential clients began calling his office. Leal hired an anti-piracy company that has helped remove nearly 6,500 fake profiles across social media, including 3,500 on TikTok, 2,400 on Facebook, and 544 on Instagram. He has changed his personal phone number and plans to contact local and federal authorities this week to investigate the scams. Leal is warning immigrants to verify anyone offering legal services online and to be cautious of social media advertisements promising immigration benefits.
